latest_release.name: 0.8.0rc1
latest_release.body: # oMLX 0.8.0rc1 > This is a release candidate. Please report any bugs through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/issues/new/choose). If you need a stable release, please use [oMLX 0.7.3](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/releases/tag/v0.7.3). The release candidate for oMLX 0.8.0 adds the Prefill Accelerator, which lets a PC with NVIDIA GPUs or a second Mac speed up prefill for a big model on your Mac, and makes DeepSeek V4.1 faster with many requests and on clusters. **Download:** [macOS 26 / 27](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/releases/download/v0.8.0rc1/oMLX-0.8.0rc1-macos26-27.dmg) | [macOS 15 Sequoia](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/releases/download/v0.8.0rc1/oMLX-0.8.0rc1-macos15-sequoia.dmg) * If you downloaded build 3727 right after release, the Cluster tab may not find a DGX Spark or NVIDIA PC, so please download it again. ## Prefill Accelerator with NVIDIA GPUs or a Mac A PC with NVIDIA GPUs, a DGX Spark or a second Mac with a faster GPU runs the first layers of each prompt chunk, while your Mac runs the rest, decodes and keeps the KV cache. Auto picks how many layers the helper takes from the measured speed of both machines and the link, and keeps the prompt on the Mac when a split would be slower (#5065, #5163, #5195). The CUDA helper builds on the great CUDA kernels of [TensorFold](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold) by @ashhart and [mlx-serve](https://github.com/ddalcu/mlx-serve) by @ddalcu, and would not have been possible without them. Thank you both for sharing them in the open. The adapted kernels and their licenses are in [`third_party/`](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/tree/v0.8.0rc1/apps/omlx-cuda-helper/omlx_cuda_helper/third_party). > Prefill tok/s on a 64K prompt, oQ4e models, M3 Ultra 512GB with a CUDA helper over 2.5 GbE. Decode speed stays about the same. | Model | M3 Ultra alone | + DGX Spark | + 2x RTX A6000 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.8 27B | 352 | 1,062 (+202%) | 1,879 (+434%) | | Qwen3.8 Flash-Next | 1,370 | 2,715 (+98%) | 3,928 (+187%) | | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 1,085 | 2,412 (+122%) | 1,914 (+76%) | | GLM-5.3 Flash | 555 | 1,076 (+94%) | 978 (+76%) | | MiniMax M3.1 Flash | 312 | 504 (+62%) | 468 (+50%) | Turn on Global Settings > Advanced > Enable Distributed Inference, pair the helper in the Cluster tab, then pick it under Prefill Accelerator in the model's settings ([guide](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/blob/v0.8.0rc1/docs/experimental/prefill-accelerator.md)). An NVIDIA PC needs only the command below and the code from `docker logs omlx-helper`, with no SSH or oMLX install. It needs driver 580 or newer and an Ampere or newer GPU or a GB10, and has not been tested on Windows yet. ``` docker run -d --name omlx-helper --restart unless-stopped --gpus all --network host -v omlx-helper:/data jundot/omlx-cuda-helper ``` ## Faster DeepSeek V4.1 with Many Requests and Clusters With the DSpark drafter on, DeepSeek V4.1 now verifies the drafts of several requests together, so the drafter keeps its speedup as requests add up (#5154).
